cls: Serotonin (5-HT2) antagonist with antihistamine and antimuscarinic activity
quick: 1.5 mg/day (range 0.5-3 mg); often single nocturnal dose
Take with or without food; bedtime dosing helps sedation
Avoid unless clearly necessary; limited data
summary: Pizotifen is a serotonin (5-HT2) receptor antagonist with antihistaminic and antimuscarinic properties used for the prophylaxis (prevention) of recurrent migraine and of cluster headache. It is not FDA-approved in the US (used in the UK, Europe and Australia as Sanomigran); this record is based on BNF/EMA/SmPC-style references. It is taken regularly to reduce attack frequency, not to treat an acute attack. The usual adult dose is 1.5 mg/day (range 0.5-3 mg/day), frequently given as a single dose at night because the main adverse effects are drowsiness and increased appetite with weight gain; antimuscarinic effects such as dry mouth can also occur.
indications: Prophylaxis of recurrent migraine (including classical and common migraine)
Reduction of frequency and severity of migraine attacks (preventive therapy, not acute treatment)

dosage.d: 1.5 mg/day; may give as a single nocturnal dose or in divided doses
dosage.t: Once at night or in divided doses

dosage.d: 0.5-3 mg/day; maximum 3 mg/day (single dose not to exceed 1 mg, except the nocturnal dose up to 3 mg)
dosage.n: Start low and increase gradually to limit drowsiness

dosage.d: Lower doses up to ~1.5 mg/day per body weight/age, per local label
dosage.n: Specialist guidance; not all labels approve pediatric use

dosage.d: Begin at a low dose (e.g., 0.5 mg) and titrate upward over days

admin: Take regularly for prevention - it does NOT relieve an acute migraine attack
A single daily dose is best taken at night to reduce daytime drowsiness
Start low and titrate up gradually; allow several weeks to assess benefit
Avoid abrupt withdrawal after prolonged use; reduce gradually
Counsel about weight gain/appetite and avoid sedatives and alcohol
moa: Pizotifen is structurally related to the tricyclic antidepressants and acts mainly as an antagonist at serotonin (5-HT2, and 5-HT1) receptors, with additional antihistaminic (H1) and weak antimuscarinic activity. By blocking 5-HT2 receptor-mediated effects on cranial vasculature and pain pathways it reduces the frequency and severity of migraine attacks; its antihistaminic action accounts for sedation and appetite stimulation.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to pizotifen or any excipient
monitor: Antimuscarinic effects (dry mouth, constipation, urinary symptoms)
Clinical response (attack frequency) over several weeks

preg: Should be avoided in pregnancy unless clearly necessary, as there are limited data on safety; weigh benefit against risk and follow current BNF/SmPC guidance.
lact: Not recommended during breastfeeding; pizotifen and its antimuscarinic/antihistaminic effects may be passed to the infant and data are insufficient.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is defined; use with caution in renal impairment and monitor for accumulation of adverse effects.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment as metabolism may be affected; titrate carefully and monitor tolerability.

major: MAO inhibitors - avoid concomitant use (as with related antidepressant-type drugs)
moderate: CNS depressants, sedatives, hypnotics, alcohol - additive sedation
Other antimuscarinic/anticholinergic drugs - additive antimuscarinic effects
Antihypertensives - pizotifen may reduce the effect of some (e.g., adrenergic neuron blockers)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no specific food interaction is established.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol - it markedly increases drowsiness and sedation.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory interference reported at usual doses.

serious: Lowering of seizure threshold in susceptible patients
rare: Anxiety, aggression or CNS stimulation (especially on withdrawal in children)
emergency: Signs of severe allergic reaction (facial/throat swelling, breathing difficulty)

monitoring: Sedation/drowsiness and impact on driving and daily activities
Appetite and body weight over time
Antimuscarinic symptoms (dry mouth, constipation, urinary difficulty)
Migraine attack frequency/severity to judge effectiveness (allow several weeks)
counsel: This medicine PREVENTS migraines when taken regularly - it does not treat an attack that has already started
Drowsiness is common - a single dose at bedtime helps; do not drive until you know how it affects you and avoid alcohol
Expect possible increased appetite and weight gain; watch your diet
Report dry mouth, constipation, or difficulty passing urine, and tell your doctor if you have glaucoma or prostate problems
Do not stop suddenly after long use - reduce the dose gradually as advised; allow a few weeks to see the benefit
pk: Preventive benefit develops over days to several weeks of regular use
Plasma peak ~5 hours after an oral dose
Long-acting; suitable for single daily (nocturnal) dosing
Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved in the US but used in the UK, Europe and Australia (Sanomigran); this record uses BNF/EMA/SmPC references
Prophylactic agent only - taken regularly to prevent migraine/cluster headache, not to abort an acute attack
5-HT2 antagonist with antihistaminic and antimuscarinic activity (structurally related to tricyclics)
KEY EFFECTS: drowsiness and appetite/weight gain - dose once at night to use the sedation and counsel on diet
Use antimuscarinic caution in glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy and urinary retention; do not withdraw abruptly
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it and continue as usual (especially if taking a single nighttime dose). Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Overdose, particularly in children, may cause drowsiness progressing to CNS depression, and antimuscarinic and stimulant effects (agitation, ataxia, fixed dilated pupils, flushing, convulsions, and possibly coma). There is no specific antidote; management is supportive with monitoring, control of seizures, and standard symptomatic care; contact a poison control center.
